title: deliveryView reads one plan's delivery view through a scope token and writes nothing; the Door serves it as next, the MCP door as ia_next and the CLI as ia next
summary: @inventarch/runtime exports deliveryView(handle, within, seat?) and NEXT_CODES from the package root and the new @inventarch/runtime/internal/next subpath, with the CycleRow, DeliveryMilestone, DeliveryResult, DeliveryTask, DeliveryView, ExitEvidence, NextCode, NextRefusal, Prerequisite, ReviewItem, StateDimension and StateLine types. deliveryView reads through the scope token within and writes nothing; only a whole-workspace token (db isCompleteScope) also reads the handle's refused records and the report's COMP-PARSE findings. The plan is the one a `@plan`, `@milestone` or `@task` seat belongs to or, without a seat, the only admitted `@plan` at band 100. It returns {ok: true, view}, the view being {format: ia.delivery-view.v1, revision, plan, milestones, tasks, review, next, summary}, or one refusal {ok: false, code, message, next, plans?, cycle?} whose next names one command: IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-SEAT (a seat the scope does not admit names ia next; a record that is no plan, milestone or task names ia position --seat <seat>), IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-NO-PLAN (names ia next --help), IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-AMBIGUOUS (several plans at band 100, listed in plans; names ia next --seat <the first>) and IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-CYCLE (require rows that form a cycle among tasks, milestones or both, listed in cycle as declared rows; names ia position --seat <its first task, else its first milestone> --shape sequence). Tasks come in one prerequisites-first order (Kahn's algorithm, ties by milestone then task): a task follows the tasks and milestones it requires and those its milestone requires. Each task carries a basis line per effective prerequisite (a required `@decision` has a choice or not; a required `@task` has exit evidence or not; a required `@milestone` has exit evidence of its own, or for every one of its tasks, or not; a requirement no admitted record answers blocks, and so, as unknown, does one the task or its milestone declares whose answer the scope does not read), inherited lines marked (via <milestone>); one verdict line, exit evidence recorded (<observation>, evaluator <evaluator>[, self-attributed | , self-attribution unknown]), no declared blocker or blocked (<basis>; ...); its work.status, printed as self-declared and never a basis; and five state lines: intent, definition, realizable, realized and worked. Exit evidence is an `@observation` with verdict success whose evidence.subject names the record, or which the record's work.exit-evidence names, and whose evidence.subject-revision reads current under the db handle's readiness; ExitEvidence.attribution is self when evidence.evaluator equals the identity the task's work.owner-agent names, unknown when the scope answers no owner-agent the task states or the observation records no evaluator for a task that names one, else other. No milestone is satisfied through its tasks, and the summary does not say that every task has exit evidence, while a task may go unread: on a narrowed scope, or on a whole-workspace scope while admission refuses a `@task` or a whole file. Review items name two or more live decisions grounding one record of the plan (one that another of them supersedes is not live, unless the two supersede each other in a cycle, which the item names), two accepted specs one of which supersedes the other with no replaced-scope, and, on a whole-workspace scope, each `@plan`, `@milestone` or `@task` admission refused and each file a language error refuses whole. next is ia position --seat <task> --shape sequence for the first task in order with no declared blocker, so tasks with exit evidence are skipped; it is null when every task has exit evidence or every other task is blocked, and summary says which. Limits: intent reads accepted or superseded only from a live grounding `@decision` that states a choice and an effective-revision; realizable and realized read not applicable for a task; worked reads stale only against the previous retained snapshot, and unknown rather than unobserved on a narrowed scope; a refused `@task` is never a listed task, as its milestone cannot be read, and only a whole-workspace scope names it as a review item; a requirement declared only on a record outside the scope is not read; and other refused records, such as a `@decision` or an `@observation`, are read as absent and not reported. The Door serves the view as a new MACHINE_PROTOCOL version 2 operation, next, with params {within?, seat?}: it answers {ok: true, result} with the DeliveryView deliveryView returns through the door's scope token, the initial boundary when within is omitted, or with that function's refusal unchanged, next, plans and cycle included. A version 2 operation's refusal may so carry more than {ok, code, message}, while a version 1 operation's refusal, and every refusal the Door raises itself (an unknown or mistyped parameter, a token it did not issue, an unknown operation), keep 1.1.0's shape. A door serving protocol version 1, as the CLI's machine routes do, refuses next as the unknown operation 1.1.0 refused, byte for byte, and a version 2 door's unknown-operation refusal lists read, then next, after the version 1 operations it admits. MACHINE_PROTOCOL stays version 2 and appends the next row, with since: 2 and mcp: ia_next, after read, plus one flow line; the nine version 1 rows are unchanged, and code that pins the version 2 rows or their parameters must take the new row. On a whole-workspace token the view's admission review items name the `@plan`, `@milestone` and `@task` records admission refused, with path, line and reason, so ia_next discloses them on the MCP door's whole-workspace initial scope. @inventarch/mcp-door serves an eleventh tool, ia_next, whose inputSchema is the next row's params. @inventarch/cli adds the consumer verb ia next [--seat <plan|milestone|task>] [--json]. It prints the plan and its summary, its milestones, its tasks in order, each with its verdict line, its status marked self-declared, one requires line per prerequisite and its five state lines, then the review items and the command for the next task with no declared blocker, with --root as given; with --json it prints one line {version: 1, ok: true, view}, view being the Door's result. It opens the workspace without the db cache and writes nothing. Its refusals keep the runtime's codes and messages at exit 1, and each names one command with --root as given: for a seat the workspace does not admit, ia validate when admission refused that record, else ia next --seat <the nearest admitted plan, milestone or task> when one is near, else ia next when the workspace authors one plan at band 100, ia next --seat <the first> when it authors several, and with none what a missing plan names; ia inspect <seat> for a record that is no plan, milestone or task; for a missing plan, ia validate when admission refused the plan a source holds, or with a seat the milestone or plan on the seat's way to its plan, else the records to author, then ia next again; ia next --seat <the first plan listed> for several; and the require row to remove, then ia next again, for a cycle. ia next is not a machine route: LEGACY_OPERATIONS, the usage line, ia <operation> --help and --schema and every ia scope form are unchanged. Limits: ia position, which the view's next and the runtime's IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-SEAT and IA-RUNTIME-NEXT-CYCLE refusals name, is not a CLI verb yet; the CLI prints the view's next as the view gives it and names ia inspect or ia next for those refusals instead. RUNTIME_CODES gains the four IA-RUNTIME-NEXT codes, so code that switches exhaustively over RuntimeCode must handle them. @inventarch/runtime/internal/render adds statedText(record, field), which the body reader now shares; readBody is unchanged.
